subject: grid lines appear when plotting with a tiny x / y limit range

messages.author: 8eb300c5ea2f77b3
messages.subject: grid lines appear when plotting with a tiny x / y limit range
parts:
Hi all,

I'm bumping against some kind of fundamental limit in how small x / y limits can range, where below some value white grid lines appear (even with theme_void()).

The use case for this is a mandelbrot set visualisation, which works until the user zooms to this threshold and grid lines appear. I'd like to understand why these appear and if it's possible to mitigate these — it's not clear to me whether this is due to ggplot2, the plotting device, some R tolerance / .Machine variable.

An example of these grid lines is here:

https://blmr.shinyapps.io/shinybrot/?x=-0.75883668471756,-0.75883668471733&y=0.071751883072278,0.0717518830724

Code to reproduce the effect locally:

# ------------------------------------

# devtools::install_github("blmoore/mandelbrot")
library(mandelbrot)

mb <- mandelbrot0(
  xlim=c(-0.75883668471756, -0.75883668471733),
  ylim = c(0.071751883072278, 0.0717518830724),
  iter = 500)

library(ggplot2) # tried with master@04a707ed
ggplot(mb, aes(x, y, fill = value)) +
  geom_raster(interpolate = TRUE) +
  theme_void()

# works with image
mb <- mandelbrot(
  xlim=c(-0.75883668471756, -0.75883668471733),
  ylim = c(0.071751883072278, 0.0717518830724),
  iter = 500)
image(mb, axes = FALSE)

# ------------------------------------

I'm sure this has come up before, any pointers very welcome!

Thanks,
Ben

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: grid lines appear when plotting with a tiny x / y limit range
parts:
I didn't run your code, but they're probably not grid lines, but gaps
between the geom_raster() cells.

Hadley
